title: Paramahansa Yogananda's birth chart
metaDescription: Paramahansa Yogananda's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.2° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds a trine to Jupiter at 0.5° — close enough to weld taste to expansion. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 15.2° of Capricorn is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Venus in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Sagittarius (22.9°), Venus in Sagittarius (16.7°), Mars in Aries (5.5°): thought that arrives already in motion, attraction declared rather than implied, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus to Jupiter is the closest call of the day, a trine within 0.5°. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Neptune conjunction Pluto at 0.8°, and the Sun square Jupiter at 1.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Saturn while both square the Sun. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. Mercury in Sagittarius at 22.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Aries at 5.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Libra at 12.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 5 in fire, 3 in air, 1 in earth, 1 in water by element, 4 cardinal, 4 mutable, 2 fixed by modality. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Leo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.6° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 20.8°.
